statement.p: Find the Taylor polynomials of degree n approximating \cos\mathopen{}\left(2x\right) for x near 0:

static.solution:
f(x) = \cos\mathopen{}\left(2x\right) Then f(0) = \cos(0) = 1, and f'(x) = -2\sin\mathopen{}\left(2x\right),\qquad \hbox{so}\quad f'(0) = 0, f''(x) = -4\cos\mathopen{}\left(2x\right),\qquad \hbox{so}\quad f''(0) = -4, f'''(x) = 8\sin\mathopen{}\left(2x\right),\qquad \hbox{so}\quad f'''(0) = 0, f^{4}(x) = 16\cos\mathopen{}\left(2x\right),\qquad \hbox{so}\quad f^{4}(0) = 16, f^{5}(x) = -32\sin\mathopen{}\left(2x\right),\qquad \hbox{so}\quad f^{5}(0) = 0, f^{6}(x) = (-64*cos(2*x)),\qquad \hbox{so}\quad f^{6}(0) = -64,
Thus, T_{2}(x) = 1 - 2 x^2, T_{4}(x) = 1 - 2 x^2 + {4\over3} x^4, and T_{6}(x) = 1 - 2 x^2 + {4\over3} x^4 - {4\over45} x^6.
